verdict: LIMITATIONS DOCUMENTED — no failure is attributable to a Version-C change

analysis.claim: All 7 failures and all 101 skips are caused by the absence of git-ignored Version-B local artifact trees in a fresh clone. None is a regression introduced by the C0 repository initialization, documentation, configuration or .gitignore changes.
supporting_reasoning: The Version-C repository was created by cloning Version B at the frozen tag. A git clone carries tracked files only; data/work/, data/processed/, reports/ and runs/ are git-ignored in Version B and are therefore absent here by design.
Every failure resolves to a missing file under one of those ignored trees, or to a default empty container returned in place of a manifest that does not exist.
The same tests are recorded as passing in Version B, where those trees exist on disk.
The 32 new C0 tests pass, and 1005 inherited tests pass, so the inherited codebase imports, parses and behaves correctly after the C0 changes.
analysis.root_cause_category: absent git-ignored local artifact tree in a fresh checkout

skips.note: Counts inside reason_groups are grouped by cause; the individual reasons were captured with `pytest -rs` and every one names the exact missing artifact and, where applicable, the command that would rebuild it.

limitation_statement: The full inherited suite cannot reach the Version-B pass count in a fresh Version-C clone, because 7 tests assert directly against frozen Version-B evidence files and 101 more are guarded on built artifact trees. Those trees are git-ignored by design and are not copied into Version C: Version C references Version-B artifacts by identity, not by possession. Reproducing them here would mean either mirroring 222 MB of Version-B reports plus 2.6 GB of processed data into the Version-C working tree, or rebuilding them - and Version C will build its own packages and banks from C1 onward regardless. The decision on how to resolve this is recorded as an open item rather than taken unilaterally.
options_for_the_user: A. Mirror the Version-B reports/ and data/ trees into the Version-C working tree read-only (untracked, git-ignored). Restores the inherited evidence tests. Costs ~2.8 GB and puts Version-B evidence inside the Version-C tree.
B. Gate the 7 evidence tests on the presence of their artifact, matching the skip discipline the other 101 already use. Keeps the suite green and honest, but edits inherited test files.
C. Leave as is and let the Version-C suite carry these 7 as known, documented, environment-caused failures until Version C builds its own equivalents in C3-C6.

Recommended: B, because it makes the inherited suite self-describing on any checkout and matches the convention the suite already uses everywhere else. It changes no scientific behaviour. It should not be done without your approval, since it edits inherited Version-B test files.
